newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK CEN BANK SETS TWO REV REPO TENDERS FOR FRI.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK CEN BANK SETS TWO REV REPO TENDERS FOR FRI.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) on Friday said it had set two securities reverse repurchase tenders for 10 a.m. (0900 GMT), offering to sterilise liquidity to a maximum volume of 6.77 billion crowns.
The NBS said in a statement that the operations would consist of a three-day reverse repo tender, as well as a seven-day reverse repo tender.
The NBS added the American-style tenders would have no fixed minimum rate.

"Not specifying the volume, the maximum possible volume we intend to drain in today's tenders is 6.77 billion crowns --our current portfolio is such," Peter Andresic, head of the NBS Open Market Operation Department, told Reuters.

"But I exclude the possibility that (local) banks would fail to meet the minimum reserve requirements for the ending period, in fact they will be overfulfilled due to liquidity inflows from foreign exchange," he added.

According to official NBS figures, the Slovak banking sector has a liquidity surplus, with banks' minimum reserve demands fulfilled at 101.75 percent as of Thursday, after being at 102.68 percent the previous day.
